definition_corrections.reason: The frozen inventory has only P0-01 through P0-03. D047's body and first recorded fingerprint prove P0-05 was present at registration, so the invalid reference is corrected by an append-only record instead of silently rewriting the immutable finding; P1-17 remains the valid related frozen finding.

Session forensics proved the D044-D053 immutable bodies equal their first successful registrations, while their stored fingerprint fields came from draft, summary, or trailing-newline inputs. The original entries remain byte-identical and this append-only record supplies only the canonical Rust-algorithm fingerprint for each exact invalid stored value.

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen audit followed ordinary Main Chat; independently shipped Builder and skill paths can construct provider authorization without the product PolicyRouter.
findings.title: Non-Main-Chat provider paths can self-authorize cloud execution
findings.observed_symptom: Builder can send accumulated answers and LifeModel-derived context under a caller-created PolicyAllowed request.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: PreparedProviderRequest validates shape but not provenance, while product call sites remain free to invent privacy decision ids and data routes.
acceptance: Every shipped provider start has a policy decision with verifiable provenance
Blocked or LocalOnly data never falls through to cloud
deletion_targets: Shipped provider calls using default prepare_chat_request

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen event finding did not identify a convenience provider API that discards an already-produced adapter receipt.
findings.title: Provider convenience API discards invocation receipts
findings.observed_symptom: generate_prepared returns only text, so Builder, skills and runtime layers can lose request-edge truth after a real provider call.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The API treats receipt consumption as optional even though receipt truth is part of successful execution.
acceptance: All product provider APIs return or durably consume the receipt
No product caller can select text while silently dropping receipt truth

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Ollama and settings probes were bounded, but the cloud generation adapter still owns separate unbounded HTTP behavior.
findings.title: Cloud provider HTTP boundary is not uniformly bounded
findings.observed_symptom: Cloud response bodies, error bodies, SSE frames, redirect and proxy behavior are not all governed by one network boundary.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Provider adapters construct reqwest behavior independently instead of consuming a typed provider network policy.
acceptance: Provider redirects, proxying, bodies, frames, connect, idle and total duration are bounded
Oversized and incomplete streams fail with minimal receipts
deletion_targets: Unbounded direct cloud reqwest response handling

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen vector and routing findings did not identify embedding as an independent model authority with silent semantic fallback.
findings.title: Embedding uses a second provider authority with silent fallback
findings.observed_symptom: Embedding can switch cloud to Ollama to hash without a route decision, profile compatibility check or receipt.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Embedding availability and vector compatibility are treated as implementation detail instead of persisted model-route truth.
acceptance: Embedding route and model profile are explicit and receipted
Incompatible fallback creates a rebuild-required state rather than silent mixed vectors

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Receipt projection exists, but aggregation can combine start and terminal facts from different requests.
findings.title: Multi-attempt provider aggregation can fabricate one success
findings.observed_symptom: Projection can select the first request id and any later completed receipt when multiple providers or attempts occur.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Receipts are aggregated by turn-level booleans rather than an attempt state machine keyed by request id.
acceptance: Every started request has an independent terminal or unknown state
Projection never joins facts from different request ids

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Local cancellation plumbing exists, but cancellation can drop provider and tool facts observed inside an in-flight kernel future.
findings.title: Cancellation can discard already-observed execution facts
findings.observed_symptom: Dropping the kernel future may leave only a provider_started boolean while receipts and tool observations never reach durable state.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Receipt collection is returned at future completion instead of being durably appended at observation time.
acceptance: Cancellation preserves all facts observed before abort
Unconfirmed remote state is remote_unknown and no late durable effect commits

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen tool timeout work did not model the boundary after an external request is dispatched but before its result is observed.
findings.title: ToolGateway cannot represent dispatched-but-unknown effects
findings.observed_symptom: An MCP or external tool timeout after wire dispatch can be recorded as failed or blocked and may become retryable.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Tool execution status lacks prepared, dispatched, confirmed and unknown effect states.
acceptance: Wire dispatch is recorded before waiting for response
Timeout after dispatch becomes unknown and is not automatically retried

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Event batches are now atomic internally, but canonical mutations and their event/outbox facts still span stores and transactions.
findings.title: Canonical writes and execution facts lack one transaction plus outbox
findings.observed_symptom: A crash can leave a domain write committed without its durable execution fact or projection trigger.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Each store owns local transactions but no PersistenceCoordinator owns mutation plus outbox atomicity.
acceptance: Canonical mutation and outbox row commit in one transaction
Projection replay is idempotent after crash

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: False completion was corrected, but scheduler policy provenance and per-request durable receipts remain absent.
findings.title: Scheduler has incomplete policy and provider truth
findings.observed_symptom: Scheduled generation currently hard-codes LocalOnly and only validates an in-memory collector before completing a claim.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Scheduler owns execution without consuming the same DataRouteDecision and durable event contract as product turns.
acceptance: Each scheduled provider request has policy provenance and a durable receipt
Unknown remote effects remain unknown and are reconciled before retry
deletion_targets: Hard-coded scheduler data route and in-memory-only receipt gate

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: AgentRun and events were minimized, but TaskSession, transcript, observation, LifeEvent and extended run fields still duplicate sensitive text.
findings.title: Sensitive canonical content remains duplicated across execution stores
findings.observed_symptom: User goals, transcript summaries and observation metadata can persist raw conversation or external content outside its canonical owner.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Storage schemas accept free-form strings and legacy migrations mark rows minimized before every sensitive column is transformed.
acceptance: Cross-store sentinel scan finds canonical body only at its owner
Legacy restart migration removes raw duplicates without losing references

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen minimization work did not define deletion propagation across stores that retain references or derived content.
findings.title: Deletion lacks cross-store tombstone and reconciliation
findings.observed_symptom: Deleting an AgentRun or conversation record does not reconcile related events, actions, vectors or LifeEvents.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Stores expose independent deletes without a canonical deletion event and idempotent projection cleanup.
acceptance: Canonical deletion writes a tombstone and outbox event
All projections reconcile idempotently and report lag instead of stale certainty

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: An unused second provider/fail-soft completion route was protected by symbol-presence tests despite having no product caller.
findings.title: Dormant fallback route survived behind false-green tests
findings.observed_symptom: generate_non_stream_fallback and ReAct follow-up synthesis remained compiled and tests asserted their presence.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Extraction tests treated symbol existence as behavior evidence and authority cleanup did not require a consumer map.
acceptance: Dormant symbols and duplicate observation reply fields are absent
Authority inventory and behavioral gates preserve the deletion

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: A ToolGateway helper initiated its own hard-coded Ollama synthesis, outside both tool and provider receipts.
findings.title: web.fetch helper initiated an untracked provider call
findings.observed_symptom: summarize=true could contact localhost Ollama after the governed web read without a provider policy or receipt.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Tool code combined evidence acquisition and model synthesis instead of returning untrusted content to the active TurnRuntime.
acceptance: Product tool code cannot start provider HTTP
web.fetch returns bounded untrusted evidence for authorized synthesis

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Secret migration did not bind a masked or environment credential to provider and endpoint identity.
findings.title: Provider credential could be reused across endpoint identities
findings.observed_symptom: Changing a provider endpoint while submitting a masked key could send the previously stored or environment key to the new endpoint.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Credential lookup was keyed by a global field instead of canonical provider endpoint identity and version.
acceptance: Masked credentials are reused only for unchanged canonical identity
Custom endpoint tests cannot inherit official environment credentials

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Audit encryption protected confidentiality at rest but still duplicated complete arguments and results into another durable store.
findings.title: MCP audit encrypted duplicate raw payloads
findings.observed_symptom: Arguments and tool results were copied in full into encrypted audit rows and exports.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Audit integrity was conflated with payload retention instead of storing minimal type, size and digest receipts.
acceptance: New audit rows and exports contain only minimal receipts
Legacy restart migration removes encrypted raw payload copies
deletion_targets: Raw MCP arguments and result audit columns as product payload

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen concurrency findings covered proposals and LifeModel writes, but not Builder session state split between an in-memory map and a last-writer-wins JSON store.
findings.title: Builder session had two authorities and duplicate review staging
findings.observed_symptom: Concurrent answers could overwrite each other and a double-click could stage duplicate review runs or proposals.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Builder commands treated an in-memory map and a file store as peers and lacked revision CAS plus an exclusive review claim.
acceptance: BuilderSessionStore is the only product session owner
Concurrent step commits one revision and concurrent review submission stages one batch
deletion_targets: Unconditional Builder session overwrite and removal

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: AgentRun minimization did not cover raw Builder transcripts exposed by list IPC or persisted with permissive local file modes.
findings.title: Builder session privacy boundary exposed raw unfinished answers
findings.observed_symptom: Listing unfinished sessions returned draft YAML and pending candidates, while raw Builder answers were stored in an app-managed JSON file without an explicit owner-only permission contract.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The resumable Builder domain object was serialized directly as a product read model and generic file persistence did not encode sensitivity.
acceptance: Unfinished-session IPC returns a narrow summary with no answer or candidate bodies
App-managed Builder directory and file are owner-only and retention is explicit

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Proposal CAS existed, but per-signal Builder proposals shared one model hash, copied canonical collection values, and had no typed atomic review batch.
findings.title: Builder review batch was self-conflicting and duplicated canonical LifeModel content
findings.observed_symptom: Accepting one of several Builder proposals made the rest stale; the first batch draft then copied full before and merged after collections into Proposal storage and exposed blind generic JSON editing.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Builder review modeled each field as an independent replace patch instead of one minimal candidate batch materialized atomically against a global base hash.
acceptance: One Builder review produces one atomic CAS proposal
Proposal stores candidate path and candidate only, with no canonical before or merged after copy
Generic batch JSON editing is unavailable until a typed editor and typed read model exist

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen suite did not assert that every explicit Builder question is retained with correct typed semantics or that malformed edits fail atomically.
findings.title: Deterministic Builder could discard or misparse explicit user answers
findings.observed_symptom: Several Socratic and Incremental answers were collected then dropped, correction text could be treated as confirmation, malformed arrays could partially apply, and free-text numeric parsing could assign the wrong score.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Removing provider inference left prompt, extraction and typed validation as separate incomplete maps without an answer-to-candidate coverage contract.
findings.owner_module: Deterministic Builder answer and candidate compiler
acceptance: Every displayed question has an explicit retain-map-or-remove disposition
Corrections do not advance confirmation and labeled numeric values map correctly
Candidate validation is whole-payload and range checked with no silent member loss

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Proposal atomic-claim work did not reconcile linked AgentRun projections or the split between confirmed effects and a later Proposal status update.
findings.title: Proposal, dispatch effect and AgentRun terminal facts could diverge
findings.observed_symptom: Builder runs remained WaitingPermission after review, and a confirmed effect followed by Proposal update failure could still appear pending or failed.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Proposal status, dispatch state and AgentRun status are updated as independent terminal truths without one reconciliation owner.
acceptance: All AgentRuns linked to a terminal Proposal converge idempotently
Confirmed effect with projection failure is reported as projection pending, never effect failed
Pending, accepted, rejected, unknown and postponed remain distinguishable
deletion_targets: WaitingPermission runs with terminal generated proposals

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The original duplicate-effect finding required atomic claim but did not define safe recovery for definitely-before-effect failure versus unknown post-dispatch state.
findings.title: Failed Proposal dispatch claims had no safe recovery state
findings.observed_symptom: A failed claim remained permanently owned, while treating every failure as retryable would risk duplicating an unknown external effect.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Dispatch state lacked a durable distinction between failed before effect, dispatched unknown, confirmed and projection pending.
acceptance: Definitely-before-effect failure can be released or revision-reclaimed
Unknown and confirmed effects cannot be automatically redispatched
Recovery transitions are CAS guarded and idempotent
deletion_targets: Binary failed status without effect certainty

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Deleting the generic Skill Runtime removed a second authority but left declarative plugin and registry built-ins exposed as selectable despite no TurnRuntime-native execution path.
findings.title: Skill catalog advertised capabilities that never reached TurnRuntime
findings.observed_symptom: Plugin IDs were unsanitizable and registry built-ins had no SKILL.md context source, so selecting an advertised skill either failed or ran ordinary chat without the skill instruction.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Catalog availability was inferred from write budget instead of an executable TurnRuntime-native context and output contract.
acceptance: Only skills with a captured bounded instruction in PreparedProviderRequest are selectable
Declarative plugin manifests remain inspectable but unavailable
Legacy JSON-envelope skill runtime is not revived
deletion_targets: Declarative plugin entries in product SkillRegistry
Selectable registry skills without TurnRuntime context

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: LifeModel CAS protected the canonical save but post-save daily snapshot and patch projection failures could still escape as if the canonical write failed.
findings.title: LifeModel post-commit projection errors could falsify canonical outcome
findings.observed_symptom: The canonical LifeModel changed before a daily snapshot error returned Err, permitting the Proposal path to record failure or encourage a duplicate retry.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Daily snapshots and patch records were executed inline as required tail steps instead of derived projections with degraded status and reconciliation.
acceptance: No error after canonical commit is reported as canonical failure
Snapshot and patch failures produce projection_degraded and remain reconcilable
Fault injection proves canonical value and receipt agree
deletion_targets: Inline projection as commit success criterion

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Deletion guards existed, but newly deleted commands were recorded as active paths with delete disposition instead of immutable expected-absent symbols.
findings.title: Authority inventory could describe deleted commands as still active
findings.observed_symptom: The manifest said commands were deleted while inventory entries still used an existing lib.rs path and disposition delete.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Inventory maintenance lacked a schema-level distinction between a future deletion target and a completed symbol deletion.
acceptance: Completed command deletions use host_path, former_symbol, deleted and expected_absent
Manifest, handler scan and inventory classification agree
deletion_targets: Active-path encoding for completed deleted symbols

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Atomic acceptance guards covered the shipped command path but an unused bulk helper could still mark low-risk proposals accepted without materializing their effects.
findings.title: Dormant low-risk batch acceptance bypassed effect materialization
findings.observed_symptom: batch_accept_low_risk updated Proposal status directly, so a future caller could report accepted without applying the canonical or external effect.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: A migration-era convenience API encoded decision status as if it were execution completion and survived without a product consumer.
acceptance: The unused bulk acceptance helper is deleted
No Proposal status transition can bypass dispatcher and materializer truth

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The event truth findings did not cover a database status value that was absent from the Rust ProposalStatus contract and silently decoded as Pending.
findings.title: Expired proposals could reappear as pending review
findings.observed_symptom: cleanup wrote status=expired, but deserialization fell back to Pending when Expired was not a typed enum variant.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The database lifecycle and domain state machine evolved independently with a fail-open unknown-status fallback.
acceptance: Expired is a typed non-reviewable Proposal status end to end
Unknown persisted status fails closed instead of becoming Pending
deletion_targets: Unknown Proposal status fallback to Pending

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Runtime fact tests did not cover a hand-built Proposal command response whose snake_case keys disagreed with the TypeScript camelCase adapter contract.
findings.title: Proposal command response and TypeScript adapter use different field names
findings.observed_symptom: Rust returns patch_result and reconciliation fields while acceptProposal declares patchResult; the current UI ignores the body, hiding the drift until a consumer relies on it.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The IPC boundary returns untyped serde_json objects and duplicates response shape knowledge in TypeScript.
acceptance: Rust uses a typed serde response with one naming convention
TypeScript contract and IPC schema test consume the exact serialized shape
deletion_targets: Hand-built Proposal result JSON with duplicated key naming

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen cancellation finding assumed an active runtime token; it did not cover the interval where a task is already user-visible but has not entered the cancellation registry, or manual cleanup skipped by an error return.
findings.title: Cancellation registry lifecycle is not linearized with the visible task lifecycle
findings.observed_symptom: A user can cancel a visible task before registry registration and the runtime later proceeds with a fresh token; a kernel error can also leave a ghost active entry.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Task publication, cancellation registration, cancellation intent and cleanup are separate non-atomic steps, cancel misses leave no tombstone, and cleanup is manual instead of scope-owned.
acceptance: Cancel and register have one linearizable outcome even when cancel wins before registration
A pre-registration cancel yields zero provider, tool and canonical write dispatch
Every runtime exit removes its active registry entry
deletion_targets: Cancel miss without durable in-process intent

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen write CAS and proposal claims prevent duplicate writers but do not order a local cancellation against a canonical transaction that is about to commit.
findings.title: Canonical commits are not linearized against local cancellation
findings.observed_symptom: Cancellation can win at the TurnRuntime select while a synchronous Memory, LifeEvent, Proposal or plan transaction still commits because the token never reaches the domain gateway.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Cancellation is an outer future-drop signal rather than an execution epoch or commit permit checked atomically at each canonical gateway boundary.
findings.owner_module: Turn execution epoch and canonical commit permits
acceptance: Cancel-winning interleavings cannot create Memory, Proposal, LifeEvent or plan writes
Commit-winning interleavings remain committed and are not relabeled cancelled
All product canonical gateways accept and verify a scoped execution permit

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen cancellation scope covered ordinary turns, while resume and retry replay dispatch tools directly outside TurnRuntime registration and token ownership.
findings.title: Resume and retry replay bypass TurnRuntime cancellation ownership
findings.observed_symptom: Cancelling a task can mark a replay action cancelled in storage while an already-dispatched Web or MCP call continues waiting and may retain an unknown remote effect.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Task controls act as a second execution runtime and invoke ToolGateway without entering the shared cancellation registry or request-level effect state machine.
acceptance: Resume and retry register under the same cancellation owner as ordinary turns
A hanging local tool wait ends promptly on local cancel
Dispatched external work without confirmation is receipted unknown and is not automatically retried

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen durable-event requirement did not identify cancellation finalization split between the command path and runtime or the multi-append partial receipt window.
findings.title: Cancellation terminal facts have two owners and are not persisted atomically
findings.observed_symptom: The cancel command can return a Cancelled task before durable cancellation events exist, while runtime later finalizes again and may persist only a prefix of cancel_requested, local_aborted and remote_unknown.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Task controls and TurnRuntime both own terminalization, and cancellation receipt facts are appended as independent transactions rather than one idempotent durable batch.
findings.owner_module: TurnRuntime cancellation finalizer and TurnEventStore batch
acceptance: One owner performs canonical cancellation finalization
Cancellation facts persist as one idempotent batch before frontend terminal delivery
Injected failure cannot expose a partial cancelled receipt as complete

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen cancellation scenario and current Phase2 test do not inspect the returned client-close signal, registration race, canonical stores, AgentLoop, ToolGateway or the cancel command duration.
findings.title: Cancellation acceptance test can pass without proving its stated guarantees
findings.observed_symptom: A test named for client request abortion ignores client_closed, starts its one-second timer after cancel returns, and checks only task events while unobserved canonical or external effects may continue.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The test was shaped around the current implementation and asserted declared metadata instead of independent transport, storage and concurrency evidence.
acceptance: The harness mechanically proves the client socket closes and times the entire cancel operation
Tests inspect every in-scope canonical store and external effect recorder
Registration-race, AgentLoop, tool and commit interleavings have independent negative assertions

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Proposal and scheduler claims are atomic, but Main Chat action replay still uses a load-then-transition sequence without an expected-state or replay claim.
findings.title: Concurrent resume or retry can dispatch the same queued action more than once
findings.observed_symptom: Two controls can both observe one replayable action, transition it independently and enter ToolGateway, duplicating an external read or effect.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: ActionQueueStore transition has no compare-and-swap precondition and replay lacks a durable exclusive claim and effect-certainty lifecycle.
acceptance: Concurrent resume and retry have exactly one replay-claim winner
A dispatched-unknown claim is not automatically released or replayed
Action transition and claim use expected revision or status CAS

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Typed tool contracts exist, but replay safety is still inferred from action-name strings and therefore ignores the actual manifest, idempotency key and effect receipt.
findings.title: Automatic retry safety is inferred from tool names instead of typed effect contracts
findings.observed_symptom: Actions named mcp.read_only, web.search or web.fetch can be automatically replayed even when the prior dispatch is unknown or the concrete peer does not provide idempotency.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: A migration-era allowlist encodes presumed semantics in names instead of consuming ToolManifest risk, effect and idempotency fields plus the last invocation receipt.
acceptance: Automatic retry requires a typed idempotent contract and a definitely-before-effect receipt
Remote unknown is never automatically retried
Tool names alone cannot authorize replay

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen MCP timeout finding did not cover a request whose frame was flushed before local cancellation and whose late response remains on a reused sequential transport.
findings.title: Cancelled MCP requests can contaminate a reused transport with stale responses
findings.observed_symptom: Dropping the local wait after an MCP frame is flushed leaves the child running; a late response can be consumed by the next request and misattributed.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The stdio session has neither request-level cancellation and multiplex correlation nor a quarantine/restart rule after an uncertain in-flight request.
acceptance: Cancel before flush remains not_attempted
Cancel after flush records remote_unknown and quarantines or restarts the session
A stale response cannot satisfy a later request
deletion_targets: Reuse of MCP session after dropped in-flight response
Completion-order response attribution without cancellation quarantine

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Durable terminal event work does not automatically make the product truthful because RunEvidenceView currently derives lifecycle from task, transcript and AgentRun projections without reading TurnEventStore.
findings.title: Task evidence read model ignores canonical durable turn terminal facts
findings.observed_symptom: When task or transcript projection lags after a durable cancel or unknown receipt, the product can still show running, retryable or completed from stale secondary state.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The read model predates TurnEventStore as the terminal fact owner and reconstructs lifecycle from projections without a reconciliation marker.
acceptance: RunEvidenceView consumes the latest durable terminal receipt before projections
Projection lag is represented as pending or degraded, never a contradictory lifecycle
Unsafe controls are disabled while canonical and projection state diverge
deletion_targets: Retry controls derived from stale task status

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: UUID uniqueness and AgentRun minimization were addressed, but ordinary Main Chat still creates its AgentRun only after provider and tool execution, leaving cancellation events to invent an unrelated run id.
findings.title: AgentRun begins after execution effects instead of owning the turn lifecycle
findings.observed_symptom: A turn can contact a provider and be cancelled before any AgentRun exists; the cancellation finalizer then generates a random run id that has no canonical AgentRun row and cannot be joined reliably.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: AgentRun is modeled as a post-kernel result projection rather than the execution identity created by OpenLifeTurnRuntime before any provider, tool or canonical effect.
acceptance: One canonical AgentRun exists before any provider or tool start
Provider, tool, cancellation and terminal events use that same run id
Cancellation never generates an event-only synthetic run id
deletion_targets: Post-effect AgentRun creation in kernel branches
Random cancellation_run_id fallback without AgentRun row

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Atomic event batches do not prevent two payloads from claiming the same immutable event identity, and current row decoding converts corrupted durable facts into plausible runtime values.
findings.title: TurnEventStore accepts conflicting immutable facts and fabricates corrupted rows
findings.observed_symptom: The same task, event type and object id can be appended again when its payload digest changes; malformed sequence, timestamp or payload data is returned as sequence zero, current time or null instead of a corruption state.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Event idempotency incorrectly includes the payload digest, while the durable row mapper uses lossy fallback values instead of failing closed on canonical-store corruption.
acceptance: An existing immutable identity with the same digest is idempotent and a different digest is a typed conflict that rolls back the batch
Invalid sequence, timestamp or payload JSON produces an explicit corruption or degraded error and never a synthetic fact
Fault tests prove sequence and prior facts remain unchanged after identity conflict or row corruption
deletion_targets: Utc::now, null and zero fallbacks for corrupted durable rows

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen network-policy finding covered ToolGateway ask semantics and the provider boundary finding covered transport bounds, but neither proved that shipped provider chat and status probes enforce the same policy represented by ProviderPrivacy.
findings.title: Provider network policy is reported but not enforced at shipped HTTP edges
findings.observed_symptom: ProviderPrivacy can report cloud blocked while Main Chat passes no NetworkPolicy to cloud HTTP, and opening Settings can issue an authenticated direct-reqwest provider probe even when networking is disabled or default-deny.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Network policy is interpreted independently by preflight, read models, provider adapters and settings probes instead of producing one enforced DataRouteDecision consumed at every provider HTTP edge.
acceptance: Disabled, default-deny and denylisted provider policies produce zero chat and status-probe dispatches under capture
Ask creates an explicit consent state before dispatch and ProviderPrivacy reflects the same enforced decision and receipt
Every shipped provider HTTP edge consumes NetworkClient plus the policy decision
deletion_targets: Provider adapter calls with no NetworkPolicy

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: D038 validates immutable identity during store initialization and current append calls, but the SQLite schema still permits a legacy process or direct connection to insert a conflicting immutable triple after the store has opened.
findings.title: TurnEventStore immutable identity is not enforced against bypass writers
findings.observed_symptom: A second connection can insert the same task, immutable event type and object id with a different payload digest after initialization, leaving list readers able to observe two contradictory facts.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Immutable identity is an application-level preflight check rather than a database-owned constraint shared by every writer.
acceptance: A post-open external SQLite connection cannot commit a conflicting immutable identity
Same-digest idempotency remains valid and legacy conflicts fail store initialization
Readers cannot observe two immutable facts with one logical identity
deletion_targets: Digest-dependent schema uniqueness as immutable authority

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Event payload value minimization removes free-form strings but still preserves arbitrary object key names and primitive values, so future generic or user-derived payloads can create a new sensitive metadata surface.
findings.title: TurnEventStore minimizer preserves untrusted object-key and primitive metadata
findings.observed_symptom: A payload containing a private fact in an object key, or sensitive numeric and boolean structure, can be durably copied even though string values are converted to receipts.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The event store recursively sanitizes values without a typed per-event schema or an allowlist for metadata keys and primitive fields.
acceptance: Unknown or user-derived object keys are omitted or replaced by a bounded digest receipt
Only typed allowlisted primitive fields survive for each event contract
Existing product event replay remains functional without copying raw external payload structure
deletion_targets: Untyped primitive retention in durable events

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: D004 profile correctness prevents mixed vectors, but every Memory search still scans and groups all active vector rows before a bounded candidate query, so profile validation itself can dominate latency.
findings.title: Vector profile compatibility check performs an unbounded active-row scan per search
findings.observed_symptom: Each search runs an O(N) GROUP BY over active vectors and then may compute cosine for up to 2000 candidates, allowing vector growth to stall ordinary Memory reads.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Compatibility state is recomputed from the full vector corpus at query time instead of maintained as an indexed profile summary updated with canonical vector writes and rebuilds.
acceptance: Compatibility lookup is bounded by indexed profile summary rows, not active vector count
Candidate dimension work has a strict maximum and rejects oversized provider vectors before persistence
Rebuild and deletion update the summary transactionally or mark it projection_degraded

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen A2A finding covered authentication, network policy and payload minimization, but not terminal truth when the governed reasoning provider fails.
findings.title: A2A reports Completed after governed reasoning failure
findings.observed_symptom: Layered reasoning failure can discard its trace and provider receipt while the A2A task handler still returns TaskState::Completed.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The A2A handler owns a second terminal-state projection and collapses reasoning failure into response prose instead of consuming the governed execution receipt.
acceptance: A2A provider failure preserves its attempt receipt and bounded reasoning trace
Failed or unknown A2A execution is never projected as Completed

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: BR4-D030 covers Main Chat task-control resume and retry, but a separate shipped AgentRun replay command and frontend bridge also invoke ToolGateway directly with non-consuming permission semantics and no TurnRuntime cancellation owner.
findings.title: Shipped AgentRun replay command bypasses TurnRuntime and durable effect ownership
findings.observed_symptom: AgentRunDetail or Chat can replay a needs_confirmation action repeatedly outside the canonical replay claim, cancellation registry, durable tool receipt projection and canonical-write admission path.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: A legacy AgentRun convenience command remained a product execution authority after Main Chat task controls and ToolGateway governance were introduced.
acceptance: No shipped command or frontend bridge can directly replay an AgentRun action outside the canonical replay claim
Replay consumes the correctly scoped permission exactly once and records pre-dispatch, dispatched, confirmed or unknown truth under one cancellation owner
AgentRunDetail and Chat consume the same task-control or ReviewWorkflow projection instead of a second runtime

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The same-proposal dispatch claim does not prevent distinct but semantically equivalent Memory proposals from committing duplicate canonical facts.
findings.title: Equivalent accepted Memory facts have no canonical uniqueness or CAS
findings.observed_symptom: Concurrent or repeated equivalent Memory proposals can each commit a new canonical Lifecycle record despite a compatibility-store duplicate precheck.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: MemoryLifecycle admission assigns a random identity and has no normalized fact key or uniqueness constraint; its duplicate precheck reads a derived compatibility store outside the canonical transaction.
acceptance: Equivalent facts derive a deterministic canonical fact key
Concurrent distinct proposals create at most one active canonical fact
The losing proposal resolves idempotently to the existing canonical owner reference
deletion_targets: Compatibility-store duplicate precheck as write authority

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Canonical gateway routing alone does not make a user-triggered Memory indexing command idempotent across double-click, IPC retry or a lost response.
findings.title: Manual Memory indexing has no retry idempotency identity
findings.observed_symptom: Repeating the same manual indexing command can create duplicate canonical Memory rows and duplicate logical outbox work.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: index_memory_chunk accepts only session, content and source and performs an unconditional insert without a stable operation identity bound to a payload digest.
acceptance: A stable operation id is bound to the exact payload digest
Retrying the same operation and payload returns the original receipt
Reusing an operation id with a different payload fails closed
Concurrent identical submissions produce one canonical row and one logical outbox item
deletion_targets: Unconditional Memory insert on command retry

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The durable-store degradation contract required an explicit read-only fallback, but the MemoryStore fallback validated a table name that no current schema creates.
findings.title: MemoryStore degraded read-only fallback always rejected the real database
findings.observed_symptom: When the writable MemoryStore could not open, the read-only recovery path checked for memory_records instead of the canonical memories table and fell through to an unavailable sentinel even though the database was readable.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The recovery constructor retained a historical table name after the canonical MemoryStore schema converged on memories, and no test opened a real current database through the degraded path.
acceptance: A current MemoryStore database opens read-only and returns canonical messages when writable open is unavailable
Missing or corrupt canonical tables still fail closed
The recovery path never silently substitutes temp or in-memory state
deletion_targets: Historical memory_records table assertion in the shipped recovery path

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Builder privacy and retention work bounded exposure duration but did not bound one reply, one session, the canonical JSON file, or review-candidate amplification.
findings.title: Builder input and canonical session persistence were unbounded
findings.observed_symptom: A very large pasted answer or oversized/corrupt Builder session file could allocate and serialize unbounded memory, block the desktop process, and amplify private content on disk; an unknown mode also silently became Quick.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Builder ingress, session persistence and review admission evolved without one bounded resource contract, while invalid enum input used a permissive fallback.
findings.owner_module: Builder bounded ingress and canonical session gateway
acceptance: Oversized replies and decision batches fail before session or proposal mutation
Canonical Builder files and sessions have explicit bounded limits and oversized files fail before deserialization
Normal long answers remain supported
Unknown Builder mode fails instead of silently selecting Quick
deletion_targets: Unbounded Builder reply and review payloads

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: D012 deleted one dormant provider fallback, but a separate callerless keyword-write, reasoning-prompt and conversation-inference module remained compiled solely because an extraction test required its existence.
findings.title: Dormant conversation update module survived behind an existence test
findings.observed_symptom: Three Main Chat helpers with zero product callers remained in the shipped module graph, including keyword-based daily-goal mutation logic and conversation inference writes.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Module extraction was treated as architecture progress without a consumer map, and a symbol-presence test became the only owner of obsolete behavior.
acceptance: The callerless module and declaration are absent from the shipped crate
An absence guard and deletion inventory prevent the keyword-write and inference route from returning

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: Message idempotency and canonical gateway work did not cover mutating slash commands intercepted by ChatPage before ordinary Main Chat enters OpenLifeTurnRuntime.
findings.title: Frontend mutating slash commands bypass TurnRuntime and canonical effect receipts
findings.observed_symptom: ChatPage can add a daily goal or record state before persisting the user and assistant messages; a lost message response followed by retry can duplicate the durable effect while the conversation has only one receipt.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: A frontend convenience parser owns policy, execution ordering and success prose outside TurnRuntime, while effect commands lack a payload-bound operation identity shared with conversation facts.
acceptance: A mutating chat command has one backend-owned policy and execution path
One operation UUID binds the exact effect payload and conversation receipt
Lost responses and retries converge to one effect and truthful message projection
Frontend no longer authorizes or reports durable mutation from a page-local parser
deletion_targets: Unkeyed add_daily_goal and record_state command effects
Frontend-generated success prose without canonical effect receipt

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen D30 scenario requires a useful post-read Memory Proposal, but the implementation grants only a read capability and then lets Kernel keyword logic authorize a second action without observation-bound policy authority.
findings.title: Kernel upgrades a read-only policy decision into an unbound Memory Proposal
findings.observed_symptom: A successful read plus matching user words always creates a Memory Proposal before canonical tool evidence exists; the proposal body comes from the request rather than the observed content and the if-useful condition is not evaluated.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Conditional multi-intent was not represented in IntentFrame or PolicyDecision, so Kernel became a second action router and ReviewWorkflow accepted a task-session reference instead of a one-shot proof bound to the current canonical observation.
findings.owner_module: PolicyRouter conditional post-observation plan and ReviewWorkflow
acceptance: D30 is represented as one exact read grant plus one linked conditional post-observation grant without a general MemoryProposal capability
A proposal can be staged only after a successful current-turn canonical observation and one-shot policy admission
Proposal content and evidence bind to the admitted observation; not-useful content produces zero Proposal
Prompt injection, cross-run evidence, cancellation and retries cannot create a late or duplicate Proposal
Buffered and streaming turns expose the same durable observation and review facts
deletion_targets: Kernel read-success plus keyword proposal branch
User-request fallback as conditional proposal body authority

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: BR4-D049 covers the genuinely callerless conversation-update helpers. ProposalEngine was a different shipped product authority with AppState, bootstrap, Main Chat finalizer and replay consumers; merging it into D049 hid the real dependency and capability change.
findings.title: ProposalEngine deletion was misclassified as callerless despite shipped consumers
findings.observed_symptom: Active deletion documents and inventory claim zero production consumers and no ReviewWorkflow admission, while the baseline product created the engine at bootstrap, invoked it after ordinary Main Chat and replay, then submitted its caller-shaped proposals to ReviewWorkflow.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Deletion evidence was written from current symbol scans without reconstructing the baseline consumer graph, so removal of an unauthorized product authority was described as dead-code cleanup and received no capability non-regression matrix.
findings.owner_module: Single-system deletion inventory and proposal capability evidence
acceptance: Active docs describe the real baseline consumer graph and the PolicyRouter authorization bypass accurately
Inventory records every former product owner and caller as expected absent
Production-wide absence guards cover state, bootstrap, finalizer, replay, reexports and semantic post-hoc proposal authorization
Ordinary provider or assistant output cannot create a post-hoc Proposal
Explicit low-risk, sensitive review-only, inferred deferred review and typed Builder/Tool permission capabilities each have separate non-regression evidence
BR4-D051 D30 remains separate and receives no ProposalEngine replacement credit
deletion_targets: Post-hoc raw run output as proposal authorization

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: BR4-D052 corrects the deleted ProposalEngine evidence and requires capability non-regression, but it does not cover the current replacement behavior that blocks the answer and creates one proposal per inferred candidate. Frozen MEM-04 and the Phase 3 contract explicitly require non-blocking deferred review and batching.
findings.title: Inferred memory governance blocks answers and emits per-candidate proposals
findings.observed_symptom: An inferred preference or stable-fact turn exits through a fixed governance-plan answer instead of the normal conversation, then stages one Proposal per candidate; implicit candidates are described as user-requested and canonical duplicates are not checked before proposal creation.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Candidate extraction, action routing and ReviewWorkflow submission were fused into a terminal Kernel strategy, so the existence of any memory artifact preempts ProviderGeneration and the materializer loop treats candidates as independent proposals rather than one deduplicated domain review batch.
findings.owner_module: PolicyRouter inferred-memory plan and ReviewWorkflow batch admission
acceptance: MEM-04 produces the normal helpful answer and does not block ProviderGeneration
All eligible inferred candidates in one domain and conversation become at most one deferred ReviewBatch
Canonical fact keys suppress or reuse duplicate pending/accepted facts before staging
Implicit candidates are never described as an explicit user request
No canonical Memory or HS change occurs before acceptance
Sensitive, identity, injected, unstable and low-confidence variants remain review-only, blocked or no-op as specified
Proposal fatigue and capability success metrics remain within the frozen thresholds
deletion_targets: run_memory_governance_turn as a terminal inferred-memory strategy
Per-candidate ReviewWorkflow submit loop for inferred memory
Proposal staging without canonical fact-key deduplication

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: D050 bound the Task receipt to raw durable columns, but the same final owner graph still deserializes Transcript and ActionQueue enum values through lossy fallbacks before hashing; the frozen migration and truth findings did not cover same-object and same-digest corruption through persisted enum coercion.
findings.title: Persisted final-owner enum fallbacks erase corruption and preserve digest equality
findings.observed_symptom: An unknown Transcript kind can reopen as a legitimate Error entry, and an unknown Action replay certainty can reopen as dispatched_unknown; both produce the same typed object and final-owner digest as the legal value. Unknown Task strategy and status values also reopen as apparently valid product state before the first final receipt is written.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Canonical store row decoders use permissive wildcard defaults and a current-schema rewrite instead of strict one-to-one persisted enum parsing, so corruption is normalized before validation and durable receipt construction.
acceptance: Every persisted Task strategy, Task status, Transcript kind and Action replay certainty has an explicit one-to-one parser and unknown values fail before typed materialization
Current-schema unknown values are never rewritten into a valid conservative state
Corrupt Transcript and Action rows cannot reproduce a legal owner object or final digest
Recovery rejects corrupt rows without provider, tool or canonical effect redispatch
All legal historical enum values retain deterministic round-trip and capability behavior
deletion_targets: Current-schema rewrite that erases unknown replay certainty

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: D050 added stable identities and owner digests, but final persistence and recovery still read independently mutable Action, Task, Transcript, Run and ToolEvent stores without one terminalization epoch; the frozen concurrency findings did not model this cross-owner final receipt race or legal post-final ReviewWorkflow successors.
findings.title: Turn finalization snapshots mutable owners without a linearization boundary
findings.observed_symptom: A Proposal accept or another legitimate owner mutation can commit between final-owner snapshots or between the last snapshot and final append, allowing a successful final receipt that immediately fails recovery. A legal post-final proposal reconciliation is also indistinguishable from unproven owner drift because recovery requires current mutable heads to equal the historical final snapshot.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: TurnRuntime constructs a terminal fact from sequential cross-store reads and appends it later, while product writers mutate the same owner graph through direct store APIs with no shared terminalization epoch, CAS transition receipt or proven successor model.
findings.owner_module: Turn owner graph gateway and durable terminalization coordinator
acceptance: Each operation has one durable open, sealing and sealed terminalization epoch bound to the immutable final event
Final append and sealed epoch commit atomically inside the event store transaction
Every production mutation of Action, Task, Transcript, Run and ToolEvent enters one gateway with expected revision or transition receipt; direct product writers are absent
Proposal review cannot race an unsealed origin turn, and a legal post-final review change is represented as a provenance-bound successor without rewriting final
Barrier tests prove snapshot-to-append and recovery races cannot create false success, false drift or duplicate redispatch
No shared store guard is held across provider, tool, network or user await, and lock order is mechanically fixed
Legacy receipts remain explicitly strict or migrated; unknown history is not silently accepted
deletion_targets: Sequential unlocked owner snapshots followed by a later final append
Direct product mutations that bypass the turn owner graph gateway
Current-head equality as the only historical final recovery rule

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen evidence findings require mechanical proof, but did not define one executable append-only registry path that canonicalizes fingerprints, owns the classification taxonomy, and proves that the guard actually executed after every registry edit.
findings.title: Discovered-finding registry admitted invalid fingerprints and an incomplete taxonomy guard
findings.observed_symptom: D044 through D053 retained their first immutable definitions but carried fingerprints that did not match the Rust canonical algorithm, D052 used a legitimate classification rejected by the guard, and an incorrectly filtered Cargo invocation executed zero tests while appearing successful.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Finding definitions, fingerprint generation, classification validation and evidence commands were maintained through separate ad hoc steps, so draft hashes or newline-bearing hashes could be recorded without immediately running the one authoritative gate.
acceptance: Every effective registry fingerprint equals the canonical no-trailing-newline Rust digest; a noncanonical stored historical value is accepted only through an exact append-only correction bound to the trusted immutable prefix
The first recorded immutable finding bodies remain unchanged while incorrect derived fingerprint metadata is corrected with provenance
The classification taxonomy has one explicit schema-owned allowlist that includes evidence_gap_and_scope_correction
Every registry edit runs a command that executes the named Phase0 test rather than matching zero tests
CI compares against the merge base and rejects deletion, reordering or immutable-body rewrite while allowing append-only findings and dynamic trace updates
deletion_targets: Ad hoc draft or summary fingerprint generation
Classification tokens duplicated outside the Phase0 schema guard
Zero-test Cargo invocations accepted as registry evidence

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen MCP audit finding covered encryption and rotation semantics, but not the shipped authority-file loader that aliases a missing file, an unreadable file and malformed JSON before bootstrap creates and persists a replacement key epoch.
findings.title: Malformed MCP audit keyring is treated as first boot and overwritten with new authority
findings.observed_symptom: A malformed or unreadable mcp_audit_keys.json becomes an empty keyring, bootstrap creates a new keychain epoch and rewrites the file, and historical audit rows can remain visible only as decrypt-failed placeholders while the original key references are no longer configured.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: The key-reference loader returns an untyped empty vector for every read or decode failure, hydration silently deduplicates epochs and treats empty as first boot, and bootstrap activates key material without proving that the reference file and existing audit database agree on the complete epoch set.
acceptance: Missing, present-valid, present-invalid and unreadable keyring states remain distinct
A present-invalid keyring or a missing keyring beside an existing non-empty audit database creates no secret, performs no rotation or overwrite, and enters explicit unavailable or read-only state
Duplicate or structurally invalid epochs fail instead of being deduplicated
A genuine first boot creates exactly one durable key reference and all configured historical epochs remain readable
deletion_targets: Automatic key creation when an existing audit database has no proven keyring
Missing-epoch fallback to the active audit key

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen tool and persistence findings did not distinguish pre-ToolGateway governance blockers from runtime-issued tool receipts, while finalization still assumes every rendered tool-call receipt has one durable terminal ToolEvent owner.
findings.title: Pre-ToolGateway blockers mint non-authoritative tool receipts that finalization treats as durable terminal owners
findings.observed_symptom: A missing workspace file or lexical traversal is blocked before ToolGateway, but Kernel manufactures a caller-only failed-before-dispatch receipt; regular event projection excludes that non-runtime receipt while final persistence requires a matching terminal ToolEvent and fails with turn_final_tool_terminal_owner_missing.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Pre-gateway blockers, live ToolGateway receipts, ActionQueue owners and durable ToolEvent owners are modeled as a positional one-to-one set, while regular projection and final recovery use different receipt-admission predicates and fallback code manufactures render-only receipt authority.
findings.owner_module: ToolGateway blocker and terminal-owner projection contract
acceptance: Missing-file and traversal admission failures return a structured blocker with failed ActionQueue state, zero Proposal and no synthetic ToolExecutionReceipt or ToolEvent owner
A real quoted or successful workspace read enters ToolGateway and owns exactly one runtime receipt and terminal event
A runtime-issued receipt with a missing, duplicate or conflicting terminal owner fails closed
Buffered, streaming and durable final recovery retain the same keyed blocker and tool-owner truth
deletion_targets: Production failed_before_dispatch receipt creation in blocked_kernel_read_tool_execution
Missing-receipt fallback that manufactures a fake tool owner
Positional ActionQueue-count equals receipt-count equals terminal-event-count recovery assumption
Pre-gateway blocker metadata carrying a synthetic toolExecutionReceipt

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen database and migration findings did not cover malformed required or present-optional JSON being decoded as null, absence or an empty collection before canonical identity, governance, migration and projection decisions.
findings.title: Canonical persisted JSON corruption is normalized into valid domain defaults
findings.observed_symptom: Legacy transcript metadata can be rewritten from malformed JSON to null while its payload version advances; Patch, Proposal, Memory and MemoryLifecycle rows can reopen with corrupted before, after, tags, evidence, conflict or rollback arrays silently replaced by legal empty values.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Canonical row decoders and one legacy migration use ok, unwrap_or_default or unwrap_or(null) instead of distinguishing SQL NULL from present-invalid JSON, and downstream projections can swallow the resulting store error into a healthy empty read model.
findings.owner_module: Strict canonical JSON row decoders and degraded projections
acceptance: Required and present-optional canonical JSON fail before typed materialization, identity digest, effect dispatch or migration version advance
A mixed valid-and-corrupt legacy migration rolls back the whole batch and preserves the original bytes for reconciliation
Canonical and audit owners never synthesize null, absence or empty arrays from a decode error
Derived views may rebuild but expose projection-degraded rather than healthy empty truth
Review and LifeState projections propagate owner decode failure as unavailable or unknown instead of ok with zero items
deletion_targets: Malformed legacy transcript metadata to JSON null migration
Patch before and after JSON semantic defaults
Memory tags JSON to empty tags
MemoryLifecycle canonical and rollback JSON to empty arrays

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: The frozen plugin and tool-authority findings did not cover the persisted user enable override being lost on read or parse failure; current plugin tools are intentionally non-executable, so the confirmed impact is product permission truth rather than a proven tool side effect.
findings.title: Malformed plugin enable overrides restore manifest defaults as valid product state
findings.observed_symptom: If enabled_overrides.json is malformed or unreadable, PluginRegistry starts with an empty override map and a manifest carrying enabled true is listed as enabled even when the user had durably disabled it.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: PluginRegistry construction erases the error with unwrap_or_default, reload cannot distinguish a missing override file from corrupt authority, and bootstrap registers the registry read-write because manifest reload itself succeeds.
acceptance: Missing override and present-invalid or unreadable override states remain distinct
Corrupt authority never restores a manifest default as a trusted user enable decision
Registry and product read models expose unavailable or unknown while preserving the original override bytes
Valid enable and disable overrides survive restart
Plugin tools and skills remain absent from executable product registries until a separate reviewed ToolGateway contract exists
deletion_targets: Plugin enable-override load error to empty map
Product read-write registration after override authority failed to load

findings.why_not_fully_subsumed: BR4-D054 covered persisted Main Chat Task, Transcript and ActionQueue enums only; PatchStore, ProposalStore and MemoryLifecycle retain separate enum and timestamp coercions whose current-schema, legacy-schema and read-only reachability require their own RED audit.
findings.title: Non-JSON persisted enum and timestamp defaults can fabricate valid owner state
findings.observed_symptom: Unknown Patch operation, source, risk or status values reopen as Replace, Manual, Medium or Pending; unknown Proposal type or risk becomes Unsupported or Medium; malformed optional timestamps disappear or MemoryLifecycle timestamps become the current time.
findings.root_cause_hypothesis: Several owner row decoders reuse permissive domain parsers or inline wildcard defaults for persisted input, and optional timestamp parsing collapses present-invalid text into absence or Utc::now instead of a database conversion failure.
findings.owner_module: Strict non-JSON canonical owner row decoders
acceptance: Every persisted enum has an explicit one-to-one database parser and unknown values fail before typed materialization or owner digest
Present-invalid timestamps fail instead of becoming None or the current time
All legal historical enum and timestamp values retain deterministic round-trip
Current schema constraints, legacy schemas and read-only recovery paths are audited separately
No D054 or D059 evidence is reused as closure credit for this owner set
deletion_targets: Patch unknown operation, source, risk and status defaults
Proposal unknown type and risk defaults
Malformed Patch and Proposal optional timestamps to absence
MemoryLifecycle unknown status to Candidate and materialization status to NotRequired on persisted reads
